name: Duane Retraction Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Duane Retraction Syndrome

criteria.description: Congenital limitation of abduction and/or adduction of the affected eye
Retraction of the globe on attempted adduction
Narrowing of the palpebral fissure on adduction
Electromyography showing co-contraction of medial and lateral rectus muscles
Imaging evidence of absent or hypoplastic abducens nerve

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital limitation of lateral eye movement with globe retraction and palpebral fissure narrowing on adduction
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical; imaging and electromyography can support diagnosis

searchTerms: eye pulls back when looking inward
narrowing of eye opening on adduction
eyelid slit narrows when eye moves inward
palpebral fissure constriction with eye movement
strabismus with inward or outward turning

common.symptomName: Head turn or face turn to compensate for limited eye movement
searchTerms: head tilt to adjust for eye movement

common.symptomName: Upshoot or downshoot of the affected eye on adduction
searchTerms: eye moves up or down on inward gaze
vertical eye movement abnormality on adduction

occasional.symptomName: Facial asymmetry due to compensatory head posture
searchTerms: facial asymmetry due to head tilt
face looks uneven from compensatory turning

rare.symptomName: Associated systemic anomalies (e.g., Goldenhar syndrome features)

searchTerms: drooping on one side of face

imaging: MRI showing absence or hypoplasia of the abducens nerve
Orbital imaging demonstrating anomalous lateral rectus muscle innervation
genetic: Mutations in CHN1 gene in familial cases
Genetic heterogeneity with sporadic and familial forms
other: Electromyography demonstrating co-contraction of medial and lateral rectus muscles

distinguishingFeatures: Bilateral facial and abducens nerve palsy

redFlags: Sudden onset of ocular motility limitation
Progressive worsening of eye movement limitation
references: Engle EC. Duane Retraction Syndrome: A Model for Human Motor Neuron Development and Disease. Curr Opin Neurol. 2007;20(1):5-13.
Miller NR. Duane Retraction Syndrome. In: Walsh & Hoyt’s Clinical Neuro-Ophthalmology. 6th ed. 2005.
